correctness.rationale: Explicit general weighted Gram entry gives diagonal \(e^{-x}x^k/k!\). The ratio of max/min diagonals is a universal lower bound; log-concavity makes it strictly decrease before the factorial-geometric-mean radius and strictly increase afterward. Equality forces the constant basis vector into the smallest eigenspace and thereby all low Fourier moments to vanish, and these moments conversely diagonalize the Gram. For \(m=n\), unitarity forces equal weights; Newton identities force the regular polygon. Stirling and the discrete Poisson mode establish the exact leading exponential and prefactor. Test code independently evaluated 1010 finite assertions; it is supporting numerical evidence, not the proof.

originality.rationale: Strongest same-object source arXiv:1109.2171 (2011), Lemma 3.3 gives the exact diagonal Poisson spectrum for equispaced coherent states with arbitrary radius. That known spectrum, the DFT inversion and the elementary radial subproblem are not claimed as independent new spectral theory. The reviewed global statement adds arbitrary positive weights and angles and an arbitrary number \(m\ge n\), an if-and-only-if optimizer condition via circle Fourier designs, forced equal-weight regular-polygon rigidity at \(m=n\), and an oversampling-invariant exponential conditioning barrier. The fixed-angle 2011 theorem does not itself compare all weighted angular designs; other inspected sources also do not state a dominating result. Residual possibility of implicit older optimal-design theorem is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A broader older weighted unit-circle optimal-design theorem may imply the final statement, notwithstanding the inspected sources.

value.rationale: Single-radius coherent-state sampling is a natural physical and mathematical reconstruction restriction. The quantified global impossibility of improving relative condition by any increase in m, reweighting, or relocating angular nodes, the exact weighted circle-design equality set and critical-sample rigidity, plus the sharp exponential rate and polynomial prefactor supply design information beyond prior fixed equidistant reconstructions. Results do not claim noise-optimal acquisition or multi-radius optimality.
